event: UFC Fight Night 291 - Buckley vs. Malott

mike-malott-joaquin-buckley.summary: A tight first round at range: Malott's body kicks and one-twos against Buckley's lunging right hooks, scored 2-1 Buckley by Sherdog's panel. Buckley clinched early in round 2 and Malott turned him on the fence and kneed the body; when they separated Buckley ducked in to throw and Malott timed a knee to the head that sent the mouthpiece flying, and a final right hand ended it at 2:32.
mike-malott-joaquin-buckley.turning_point: Round 2: Buckley changed levels into the knee; Malott had been landing knees in the clinch moments earlier.

checks.claim: Malott's length and kicking at range, Buckley loses when he can't land the big shot
checks.note: Range was even in round 1 (Buckley took it on two of three cards); the fight was won in the clinch and on a counter knee.

checks.claim: Decision: Malott's cardio past round three unproven
checks.note: Malott finished it in round 2; the five-round cardio question never came up.
Buckley's best moments were round 1 right hooks; he was out in round 2.

jasmine-jasudavicius-erin-blanchfield.summary: Jasudavicius won the wrestling Blanchfield was supposed to own: she took Blanchfield down twice in round 1, took the back with a body triangle and cranked the neck to the horn, then did it again in round 2 after a single leg, finishing the round in mount. Blanchfield won round 3 on the feet with combinations before Jasudavicius dragged her down late: 29-28 on all three Sherdog cards and a unanimous decision.
jasmine-jasudavicius-erin-blanchfield.turning_point: Round 1: Jasudavicius's second takedown and back take; from there the bigger woman controlled every grappling exchange.

checks.claim: Blanchfield's back takes punish the wrestling exchanges Jasudavicius needs
checks.note: Jasudavicius won every grappling exchange and took Blanchfield's back twice.

cristian-perez-kyle-nelson.summary: Pérez opened with a rolling leglock attempt, stood up into a hard Nelson right hand that dropped him to a knee, and came straight back firing: a knee and a four-punch combination on the fence put Nelson down and hammerfists finished it at 0:27.
cristian-perez-kyle-nelson.turning_point: Pérez absorbed Nelson's right hand and answered immediately instead of resetting.

checks.claim: Nelson stopped in round one in both recent losses; Pérez's chance and Nelson's worst both fall early
checks.note: Stopped in 27 seconds.

marc-andre-barriault-kyle-daukaus.summary: Daukaus took Barriault down, reached mount and the back with a body triangle and hunted the choke for two minutes, but Barriault broke the triangle and stood. When Daukaus shot again Barriault met him with a knee, then a second knee that dropped him, and elbows and punches on the turtled Daukaus brought the stoppage at 4:28 of round 1.
marc-andre-barriault-kyle-daukaus.turning_point: Barriault's escape to his feet; Daukaus kept shooting into knees instead of resetting at range.

checks.claim: Daukaus's chokes against a forward-pressing brawler: SUB R1
checks.note: He got the takedown and the back exactly as expected but couldn't finish, and Barriault escaped.

timothy-cuamba-louis-jourdain.summary: After an even first two minutes of kicks, Cuamba took Jourdain down, survived a loose guillotine and dragged him back down every time he stood, ending round 1 with elbows from side control. In round 2 he worked the body, caught a kick for another takedown, trapped the wrist and punched until Jourdain gave his back, then finished with a choke at 2:48.
timothy-cuamba-louis-jourdain.turning_point: Cuamba's first takedown; Jourdain never stopped one after that.

checks.claim: Cuamba has been taken down and choked recently and struggles going backwards
checks.note: Cuamba was the one taking the back; Jourdain never got him moving backwards.

mandel-nallo-nate-landwehr.summary: Nallo controlled range from the opening exchange with his jab, front kicks and calf kicks, wobbled Landwehr with a straight right, battered him along the fence and hobbled his lead leg: a 10-8 round on every Sherdog card, ending with Nallo on the back. Two more leg kicks in round 2 dropped Landwehr and the referee stopped it at 0:47.
mandel-nallo-nate-landwehr.turning_point: The calf kicks late in round 1: Landwehr could barely stand on the leg by the bell.

checks.claim: Landwehr, 38 and moving up, has been knocked out three straight times walking forward: KO R1
checks.note: Hurt badly in round 1 and stopped early in round 2 (the round was off by one).

tanner-boser-jhonata-diniz.summary: Boser, the smaller man, took Diniz down with a single leg in every round and Diniz never stopped one. Round 1 was side control and knees, round 2 a crucifix with elbows and punches (10-8 on every card), and in round 3 Boser mounted, took the back and kept punching until Herzog stopped it at 4:26.
tanner-boser-jhonata-diniz.turning_point: Boser's first takedown in round 1 showed Diniz had no answer on the floor.

checks.claim: The bigger, rangier striker against an undersized heavyweight; trading early: KO R1
checks.note: Boser wrestled instead of trading and the size never mattered on the floor.

joel-faglier-javad-mahjoub.summary: Mahjoub surprised everyone with his hands: he dropped Faglier with a one-two, swarmed him on the fence and floored him again with a straight right, a 10-8 round on every card. But he was exhausted by the bell; Faglier went to the body in round 2, and once Mahjoub's punches lost their steam a big right hand put him down and hammerfists ended it at 2:11.
joel-faglier-javad-mahjoub.turning_point: The end of round 1: Mahjoub punched himself out trying to finish, and Faglier survived.

checks.claim: Faglier, 25 and heavier, against a 35-year-old judoka: Faglier's hands early, R1
checks.note: Faglier won late, on the older man's cardio, after nearly being finished himself in round 1.

katlyn-cerminara-mackenzie-stiller.summary: Stiller started fast with combinations and low kicks, but Cerminara settled behind her jab, check hooks and knees, and Stiller's punches started falling short. When Stiller shot a single leg late in round 1 Cerminara sprawled and punched, Stiller hit the mat under fire and the referee stopped it at 4:46: Cerminara's first finish in more than a decade.
katlyn-cerminara-mackenzie-stiller.turning_point: Stiller's desperation single leg at the fence, which put her on the mat under punches.

steven-koslow-chad-anheliger.summary: Anheliger landed the cleaner leg kicks and right hands at range, but Koslow took him down midway through every round and won the first two from top position with punches and elbows. In round 3 he got a body-lock takedown, moved through mount to the back with a body triangle and finished with a rear-naked choke at 4:31.

chelsea-chandler-melissa-croden.summary: Croden was winning round 1 clearly: she stalked, landed the one-two, elbows and knees to the body, and Chandler kept clinching to survive. With seconds left Croden tripped her in the clinch, Chandler rolled into top position and caught a kimura that she cranked until the arm gave, a submission at 4:52.

checks.claim: Croden builds late and has never been finished; Chandler is dangerous early: Croden KO R3
checks.note: Croden was out-striking her, but Chandler's early danger (the grappling, not the power) finished it in round 1.
